articles.title: EUA mobilizam Departamento de Guerra para as eleições | G1
articles.standfirst: Memorando assinado pelo secretário Pete Hegseth mira votação de novembro, quando americanos vão renovar a Câmara e parte do Senado. Documento foi divulgado nesta segunda (28).
articles.summary: Memorando assinado pelo secretário Pete Hegseth mira votação de novembro, quando americanos vão renovar a Câmara e parte do Senado. Documento foi divulgado nesta segunda (28).
articles.body:
O secretário de Guerra dos Estados Unidos , Pete Hegseth, assinou um memorando para mobilizar estruturas do governo contra “adversários estrangeiros” que possam tentar interferir nas eleições. O documento foi assinado em 22 de setembro e divulgado nesta segunda-feira (28).

A medida mira as eleições de novembro, quando os americanos irão às urnas para escolher deputados e senadores. O pleito é conhecido como “midterms”, ou eleições de meio de mandato, porque ocorre na metade do mandato do presidente Donald Trump. Entenda mais abaixo.

Segundo o Departamento de Guerra, o Comando Cibernético dos EUA e outras agências vão trabalhar para identificar, interromper e neutralizar possíveis interferências estrangeiras nas eleições.

No memorando, Hegseth também determinou que as agências de inteligência realizem operações de coleta e produção de informações sobre “ameaças estrangeiras” às eleições dos Estados Unidos. Nenhum país foi citado nominalmente.

“Na América, o povo governa — e precisamos garantir que a voz do povo permaneça soberana, segura e totalmente livre de interferências”, diz o documento.

O secretário Pete Hegseth ao lado de Donald Trump durante reunião de gabinete em 26 de março de 2026. — Foto: Sipa USA via Reuters

A medida foi anunciada a pouco mais de um mês das eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA. Em novembro, os americanos vão escolher todos os 435 deputados da Câmara dos Representantes e uma parte dos senadores.

O resultado pode mudar o equilíbrio de forças no Congresso. Hoje, os republicanos, partido de Trump, controlam a Câmara e o Senado.

Por outro lado, pesquisas mostram os democratas podem tomar o controle da Câmara e reduzir a vantagem dos republicanos no Senado. Isso poderia prejudicar a governabilidade de Trump.

Para tentar impedir o avanço da oposição, o presidente incentivou o redesenho de mapas eleitorais em alguns estados para favorecer candidatos republicanos nas eleições. As mudanças foram questionadas na Justiça.

articles.title: Daniel Vilela promete auxílio a mulheres vítimas de violência em GO | G1
articles.standfirst: O candidato andou junto com apoiadores na região norte de Goiânia. Ele falou em ampliar o investimento em vídeo monitoramento e ferramentas de inteligência artificial.
articles.summary: Daniel Vilela promete auxílio financeiro a mulheres vítimas de violência em Goiás e defende uso de inteligência artificial na segurança pública estadual durante agenda em Goiânia.
articles.body:
O candidato ao governo de Goiás, Daniel Vilela ( MDB ), cumpriu agenda na região norte de Goiânia nesta segunda-feira (28). Durante a caminhada, ele prometeu ajuda financeira para mulheres vítimas de violência doméstica, apontando que o medo da vulnerabilidade financeira é um dos principais fatores que impedem as denúncias contra agressores.

"Nós queremos aperfeiçoar isso, trazer cada vez mais inteligência para esses programas, além de criar uma rede segura para poder amparar as mulheres sob todos os aspectos. Combatendo o feminicídio, garantir a elas o apoio financeiro, que é um dos fatores mais relevantes e que geram mais receio nas mulheres ao decidirem denunciar seus agressores", disse.

Daniel começou o dia na Avenida Goiânia, no Jardim Guanabara, onde foi recebido por apoiadores e caminhou durante duas horas ao lado do ex-governador e candidato à presidência Ronaldo Caiado ( PSD ) e do prefeito de Goiânia, Sandro Mabel ( União Brasil ). O candidato cumprimentou eleitores, tirou fotos e entrou em diversos comércios da avenida.

Ele também falou em ampliar o investimento em videomonitoramento e ferramentas de inteligência artificial para reforçar a segurança dos comerciantes do estado. Na área social, Daniel Vilela disse que, se reeleito, vai ampliar as políticas de qualificação profissional para melhorar as condições de vida de famílias em situação de vulnerabilidade.

"Seiscentas mil famílias deixaram a condição de extrema pobreza ao longo desses últimos sete anos e meio", afirmou.

“A gente tem água, a gente tem café, a gente tem uma produção muito legal no Espírito Santo que tem que ser fomentada através dessa rede de infraestrutura: porto, rodovia, ferrovia, conexão com Minas, conexão com o estado do Rio de Janeiro, conexão com a Bahia. O Espírito Santo é um estado pouco falado, ao mesmo tempo, um estado que conecta três estados sensacionais e centrais no Brasil, por ter uma posição única aqui".

articles.title: Renan Santos afirma que vai 'resolver problema do STF' | G1
articles.standfirst: Ao criticar os integrantes da Corte, candidato à Presidência pelo Missão afirmou que ministros são corruptos e 'saem completamente da casinha'. Ele esteve em Vitória nesta segunda (28) em agenda de campanha.
articles.summary: Ao criticar os integrantes da Corte, candidato à Presidência pelo Missão afirmou que ministros são corruptos e 'saem completamente da casinha'. Ele esteve em Vitória nesta segunda.
articles.body:
Em agenda de campanha em Vitória na noite desta segunda-feira (28), o candidato à Presidência da República Renan Santos (Missão) defendeu uma reformulação no Judiciário e declarou que pretende "resolver o problema” do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ).

O candidato sustentou, ainda, a retomada do cumprimento de pena de forma imediata após condenação em segunda instância.

Ao criticar os integrantes do STF, Renan Santos afirmou que a Corte é corrupta e "sai completamente fora da casinha [...] tomando mais do que deveria, [com] um ministro passando por cima do outro".

A execução provisória da pena em segunda instância deixou de ser aplicada pelo STF em 2019 , quando o plenário da Corte decidiu que a prisão só pode ocorrer após o trânsito em julgado de todos os recursos , em respeito ao princípio constitucional da presunção de inocência.

Questionado sobre suas propostas para o Espírito Santo, Renan afirmou que o estado se tornou uma rota de passagem do crime organizado entre o Rio de Janeiro e a Bahia, e mencionou ações do Comando Vermelho na Região Metropolitana capixaba.

Para a segurança pública, o candidato propôs a "destruição do crime organizado", a aprovação de leis penais mais rigorosas e o enfrentamento à "indústria das multas aos municípios".

"As facções, infelizmente, invadiram vários estados do Brasil e aqui é uma área de passagem entre Rio e Bahia. Infelizmente o Comando Vermelho vem para cá, traz o terror. Já passamos por muitos momentos difíceis, não só em Vitória, mas em Serra e outros lugares ao redor da capital".

Renan Santos cumpriu agenda de campanha no Espírito Santo nesta segunda-feira (28) — Foto: Reprodução/TV Gazeta

Infraestrutura, turismo e polo fabril portuário

Durante a passagem pelo estado capixaba, o candidato elencou outras propostas voltadas para o desenvolvimento regional capixaba:

Turismo: afirmou que "Vitória é a nova Florianópolis" e defendeu um plano de investimentos para as próximas duas décadas com foco na infraestrutura da orla e na projeção internacional da gastronomia capixaba.

Infraestrutura: defendeu a ampliação de rodovias, ferrovias e estruturas portuárias para escoar a produção do agronegócio e do café, reforçando a integração com Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro e Bahia.

Desenvolvimento industrial: propôs cortes nos gastos do governo federal para redução da taxa de juros, visando financiar a instalação de um polo fabril tecnológico ao redor do Porto de Vitória.

Ao abordar a gestão da economia, o candidato citou publicações internacionais para chancelar suas propostas: "A revista The Economist já deixou claro: eu sou o único capaz de resolver os problemas econômicos do Brasil".

Comentando o cenário político nacional e o escândalo envolvendo o Banco Master, o candidato voltou a fazer acusações contra lideranças de campos opostos: "O Brasil não pode ser governado por dois corruptos (...) Lula e Flávio são bandidos. Me coloque lá que eu desmascaro essa gente".

articles.title: Raquel Lyra promete deixar Delegacias da Mulher funcionando 24 horas | G1
articles.standfirst: Governadora e candidata à reeleição pelo PSD cumpriu agenda na comunidade de Caranguejo Tabaiares, no Recife, e falou sobre propostas para enfrentamento à violência de gênero.
articles.summary: Governadora e candidata à reeleição pelo PSD cumpriu agenda na comunidade de Caranguejo Tabaiares, no Recife, e falou sobre propostas para enfrentamento à violência de gênero.
articles.body:
A governadora e candidata à reeleição Raquel Lyra ( PSD ) cumpriu agenda de campanha nesta segunda-feira (28) na comunidade de Caranguejo Tabaiares, no bairro da Ilha do Retiro, na Zona Oeste do Recife . Ela participou de um encontro de mulheres da localidade e falou sobre propostas para enfrentar a violência de gênero no estado (veja vídeo acima) .

A candidata chegou ao local do evento acompanhada da vice-governadora Priscila Krause (PSD), que também concorre à reeleição, e dos dois postulantes ao Senado de sua chapa, os deputados federais Eduardo da Fonte (PP) e Túlio Gadelha (PSD).

"Chegamos ao governo de Pernambuco e havia uma delegacia da mulher funcionando 24 horas, a de Santo Amaro. A gente está com nove delas funcionando, das 15. Abriremos todas as Delegacias da Mulher 24 horas. Já temos 39 'salas lilás' dentro das delegacias comuns e faremos em todas elas "salas lilás" e vamos avançar para novos centros de referência ao acolhimento de mulheres vítimas de violência", disse.

Após a agenda com as mulheres, a candidata do PSD não teve mais compromisso público de campanha nesta segunda-feira e, de acordo com a equipe de campanha, reservou a agenda para a gravação de conteúdo para o guia eleitoral.

articles.summary: Confira atividades de Guilherme Fonseca (PSTU), Ivan Moraes (PSOL), João Campos (PSB), Professora Camila (UP), Raquel Lyra (PSD)  e Victor Assis (PCO).
articles.body:
Candidatos ao governo de Pernambuco nas eleições 2026 — Foto: Arte/g1

Seis dos sete candidatos ao governo de Pernambuco cumpriram agenda de campanha nesta segunda-feira (28). Entre os compromissos, houve roda de conversa, participação em podcasts, atos de rua e panfletagens em cidades do Grande Recife e do Sertão.

A governadora e candidata à reeleição, Raquel Lyra (PSD) , promoveu um encontro com eleitoras na capital. O ex-prefeito do Recife João Campos (PSB) também concentrou as atividades na Região Metropolitana, com um ato de "porta a porta" e uma minicarreata.

O candidato Renan Hallais (Missão) não divulgou seus compromissos de campanha até a última atualização dessa reportagem.

Veja como foram as agendas dos candidatos (por ordem alfabética):

Segundo agenda do candidato, Guilherme Fonseca fez panfletagem em frente a uma escola estadual da comunidade de Roda de Fogo, no bairro dos Torrões, na Zona Oeste do Recife. À noite, distribuiu panfletos na Avenida Conde da Boa Vista, no Centro da capital.

O ex-vereador do Recife concedeu entrevista à Rádio Litoral FM e participou de dois podcasts pela manhã. À tarde, gravou material para o guia eleitoral e participou de uma reunião de campanha.

Pela manhã, o ex-prefeito do Recife realizou um ato de "porta a porta" com moradores da comunidade de Roda de Fogo, no bairro dos Torrões. Durante a caminhada, ele prometeu retomar o 13º do Bolsa Família em Pernambuco e ampliar a rede de creches para combater a fome e reduzir a vulnerabilidade social.

Segundo a agenda do partido, no início da noite, participou de uma minicarreata pelas ruas de Paulista , no Grande Recife.

A candidata da Unidade Popular (UP) conversou, pela manhã, com moradores da região de Suape, no Cabo de Santo Agostinho , na Região Metropolitana do Recife. Em seguida, fez panfletagem no centro comercial do município. À tarde, distribuiu panfletos no bairro do Derby, área central do Recife.

A governadora e candidata à reeleição participou, pela manhã, de uma roda de conversa com mulheres da comunidade Caranguejo Tabaiares, no bairro da Ilha do Retiro, na Zona Oeste do Recife.

Durante o encontro, Raquel Lyra prometeu manter todas as Delegacias da Mulher funcionando 24 horas por dia e criar salas especializadas . Depois do compromisso, gravou material para o guia eleitoral.

O candidato do PCO cumpriu agenda de campanha em Petrolina nesta segunda-feira. A assessoria não informou quais foram os compromissos de Victor Assis no município.

Um resumo com as principais notícias do Jornal Nacional desta segunda-feira (28).

Uma operação contra o tráfico de drogas deixou três mortos e 13 feridos no Rio de Janeiro. Os bandidos cercaram dois ônibus com estudantes numa das principais vias de acesso à cidade. Postos de saúde e escolas públicas fecharam as portas. Temporais causaram prejuízo em 70 cidades gaúchas e avançam para outras duas regiões do país. Um bombardeio da Rússia atingiu a Academia Nacional de Ciências da Ucrânia, em Kiev. O papa Leão XIV pediu que russos e ucranianos façam concessões em favor da paz. O maior foguete do mundo chegou à órbita pela primeira vez e deu duas voltas completas na Terra. O técnico Carlo Ancelotti anunciou que vai mexer na seleção no jogo desta terça-feira contra a Austrália.

articles.title: Quaest divulga nova pesquisa da eleição presidencial; veja números | G1
articles.standfirst: A margem de erro é de dois pontos percentuais para mais ou para menos. O nível de confiança é de 95%.
articles.summary: A margem de erro é de dois pontos percentuais para mais ou para menos. O nível de confiança é de 95%.
articles.body:
A Quaest divulgou uma nova pesquisa de intenção de voto para presidente, contratada pela Globo e pelo jornal "O Globo". De acordo com o instituto, Lula lidera no primeiro turno, seguido por Flávio Bolsonaro . A margem de erro é de dois pontos percentuais para mais ou para menos. O nível de confiança é de 95%.

Lula, do PT , tinha 38% na primeira quinzena de agosto. Depois, 37%; 36% em duas rodadas; 37% de novo . Agora, 39%. Com a margem de erro, varia de 37% a 41%. Flávio Bolsonaro, do PL , tinha 31%. Depois, 29% em duas rodadas; 31%; 33%. Agora, 34%. Com a margem, tem de 32% a 36%.

Ronaldo Caiado , do PSD , tinha 4%. Depois, 1%; 3%; 4% em duas pesquisas. Agora, 4% de novo. Na margem, de 2% a 6%. Augusto Cury , do Avante , tinha 2%. Depois, 10%; 8%;7%; 6%. Agora, 4%. Com a margem, tem de 2% a 6%. Renan Santos , do Missão , tinha 4%. Depois, 3% em duas sondagens; 4%; 3%. Agora, 3%. Com a margem, tem de 1% a 5%. Romeu Zema , do Novo, tinha 2%. Depois, 1%; 2%; 1% em duas pesquisas. Agora, 1% de novo. Na margem, vai até 3%. Ronaldo Caiado, Augusto Cury, Renan Santos e Romeu Zema estão empatados dentro da margem de erro.

Indecisos eram 10%. Depois, 11%; 10% em duas pesquisas; 8%; agora, 5%. Brancos, nulos ou não vão votar: 8%; depois, 7%; 8%; 7% em duas rodadas. Agora, 10%.

Não pontuaram nessa rodada: Samara Martins , do partido Unidade Popular ; Edmilson Costa , do PCB ; Wilson Grassi , do Democrata; Clariana Barão , do partido Democracia Cristã ; Rui Costa Pimenta , do PCO ; Leonardo Avalanche , do PRTB ; e Hertz Dias , do PSTU .

Quaest divulga nova pesquisa da eleição presidencial — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

A Quaest pesquisou cinco cenários de segundo turno. No primeiro, a disputa é entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro. De acordo com a Quaest, os dois candidatos estão numericamente empatados.

Na primeira quinzena de agosto, Lula, do PT, tinha 43%. Depois, 42%; 41%; 40%; 41%; agora, 42%. Com a margem de erro, varia de 40% a 44%. Flávio Bolsonaro, do PL, tinha 40%. Depois, 41% em duas pesquisas; 42% em dois levantamentos; agora, 42% de novo. Com a margem, varia de 40% a 44%. Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro estão empatados. Indecisos: 4% em duas pesquisas; depois, 5% em duas sondagens; e 3% nas duas últimas rodadas. Branco, nulo, não vai votar: 13% em quatro levantamentos; 14%; e, agora, 13%.

Quaest segundo turno: Lula x Flávio Bolsonaro — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Outro cenário é entre Lula e Ronaldo Caiado. Lula, do PT, tinha 44%. Depois, 42%; 41% em três pesquisas; e, agora, 43%. Com a margem, varia de 41% a 45%. Ronaldo Caiado, do PSD, tinha 37% em duas pesquisas. Depois, 38%; 39% em duas rodadas. Agora, 40%. Na margem, tem de 38% a 42%. Lula e Ronaldo Caiado estão empatados dentro da margem de erro. Indecisos: 5%; depois, 4% em quatro levantamentos. Agora, 2%. Branco, nulo, não vai votar: 14%; 17% em duas sondagens; 16% em duas pesquisas. Agora, 15%.

A Quaest considerou também um cenário entre Lula e Renan Santos. Lula, do PT, tinha 44%. Depois, 43%; 42%; 41% em dois levantamentos. Agora, 42%. Com a margem, de 40% a 44%. Renan Santos, do Missão, teve 36% em duas pesquisas. Depois, 37%; 38% em duas rodadas. Agora, 39% de novo. Com a margem, de 37% a 41%. Lula e Renan Santos estão empatados dentro da margem de erro. Indecisos: 4% em cinco pesquisas; agora, 2%. Brancos, nulos ou não vão votar: 16% e 17% em cinco sondagens.

Agora, o cenário com Lula e Augusto Cury. Lula, do PT, tinha 40%; depois, 39%; 38%; 39%; agora, 42%. Com a margem, de 40% a 44%. Augusto Cury, do Avante, aparecia com 34%. Depois, 35%; 36%; 35%; agora, 33%. Com a margem, de 31% a 35%. Indecisos: 5% nessas cinco pesquisas. Votos em branco, nulos ou em nenhum dos candidatos: 21% em quatro rodadas. Agora, 20%.

Vamos ver agora a disputa entre Lula e Romeu Zema. Lula, do PT, tinha 45%. Depois, 44% em duas sondagens; 45%; 46%; agora, 46% de novo. Com a margem de erro, de 44% a 48%. Romeu Zema, do Novo, tinha 34%; 33% em três levantamentos; 32%; e, agora, 30%. Com a margem, de 28% a 32%. Indecisos eram 5%; 4% em quatro pesquisas; e, agora, 5%. Branco, nulo ou não vai votar: 16; 19% em duas rodadas; 18% em dois levantamentos; e, agora, 19%.

Quaest: aprovação governo Lula — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

A Quaest também divulgou uma pesquisa com a avaliação que os brasileiros fazem do governo e do trabalho do presidente Lula.

Na primeira quinzena de agosto, 46% aprovavam o trabalho de Lula. Depois, 45%; 43% em dois levantamentos; 44%; agora, 46%. 48% desaprovavam em duas sondagens. Depois, 50% em três pesquisas. Agora, 49%. Não souberam ou não responderam : 6%; 7% em três rodadas; 6% de novo. Agora, 5%.

A Quaest pediu que os entrevistados avaliassem o governo de maneira geral.

Na primeira quinzena de agosto, 36% avaliavam o governo Lula de maneira positiva . Depois, 35%; 34%; 32%; 33%; e, agora, 34%. Regular : 25% em três pesquisas. Depois, 27%; 23%; agora, 23% de novo. Avaliavam de maneira negativa : 37% em duas rodadas. Depois, 38% em duas pesquisas; 42%; agora, 41%. Não souberam ou não responderam : 2%; depois, 3% em três levantamentos; e depois 2% nas duas últimas sondagens.

A Quaest entrevistou 2.004 eleitores em 120 cidades, de quinta-feira (24) até domingo (27). O levantamento está registrado no Tribunal Superior Eleitoral.

articles.title: Gabriel Souza promete retirar pessoas de zonas de risco de enchente | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul pelo MDB cumpriu compromissos de campanha em Porto Alegre.
articles.summary: Candidato ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul pelo MDB cumpriu compromissos de campanha em Porto Alegre.
articles.body:
Candidato ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul pelo MDB, Gabriel Souza cumpriu compromissos de campanha nesta segunda-feira (28). Ele esteve em Porto Alegre .

O vice-governador participou de uma reunião no comitê central da campanha para alinhas as ações antes do dia 4 de outubro, quando será realizado o 1º turno das eleições. A equipe definiu as estratégias para a semana, planejando caminhadas, mobilizações e contato com eleitores que ainda não definiram seu voto.

Até o dia 2 de outubro, os candidatos ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul vão responder perguntas feitas diretamente por eleitores entrevistados pela RBS TV. Serão seis temas, um a cada semana: segurança, saúde, educação, infraestrutura, economia e prevenção a desastres climáticos . Ao todo, 86 eleitores terão suas dúvidas respondidas .

Os candidatos terão 30 segundos para apresentar suas respostas. Dos sete candidatos, três responderão em cada dia . A ordem de aparição leva em conta a mais recente pesquisa eleitoral contratada pelo Grupo RBS , divulgada nesta segunda-feira (24).

Sobre prevenção a mudanças climáticas , o candidato escolheu a pergunta da eleitora Tainá, de Lajeado , no Vale do Taquari. "A casa onde eu cresci e meus pais moram até hoje em Estrela nunca tinha sido atingida pela enchente até 2023. Em menos de 3 anos, foram 3 enchentes. Qual o seu plano de governo para reorganizar e planejar as cidades e regiões onde este evento climático tem ocorrido com mais frequência?" , questionou Tainá.

"O estado do Rio Grande do Sul tem um plano de ação para melhorar a resiliência climática, a preparação do estado para eventos como esse, que é o Plano Rio Grande. São 240 ações em andamento, já conclusas, que estão viabilizando retirada de milhares de gaúchos de zona de risco. No Vale do Taquari, por exemplo, temos vários projetos de retirada de pessoas das zonas de risco, exatamente para protegê-las, fazer com que essas zonas não sejam ocupadas e realocar as famílias. Portanto, no meu governo, vai ter celeridade sobre esse plano e não atraso no cronograma. Eu conheço cada um dos projetos, sei o que fazer, eu vou acelerá-los", afirmou Gabriel.

articles.summary: O curso gratuito em Petrolina oferece 35 vagas para mulheres interessadas em produzir itens natalinos e gerar renda extra; inscrições começam nesta terça (29).
articles.body:
Petrolina oferta curso de produtos natalinos voltado às mulheres — Foto: Ascom/PMP

A Secretaria de Assistência Social e Combate à Fome de Petrolina abre, nesta terça-feira (29), as inscrições para o curso gratuito de Produção de Itens Natalinos. Voltada para mulheres que buscam gerar renda extra no fim de ano, a iniciativa oferece 35 vagas. O cadastro deve ser feito presencialmente até quinta-feira (1º), das 9h às 14h, na Secretaria Executiva da Mulher, localizada na Rua do Cajueiro, nº 264, Centro.

Para garantir a participação, as interessadas devem apresentar RG e comprovante de residência no ato da inscrição. Com carga horária de 200 horas, as aulas serão realizadas no SENAI Petrolina de 5 de outubro a 7 de dezembro, sempre no turno vespertino.

Além de ensinar técnicas de artesanato e produção temática, a capacitação visa preparar as alunas para o empreendedorismo. O aprendizado permitirá que as participantes produzam tanto para consumo próprio quanto para a comercialização dos itens, estimulando a autonomia financeira e o desenvolvimento econômico local.

articles.title: Criança leva arma carregada para creche nos EUA; responsável foi preso | G1
articles.standfirst: Um dos pais da criança é policial, segundo as autoridades. Caso aconteceu em uma escola de Canton, no Michigan, nesta segunda-feira (28).
articles.summary: Um dos pais da criança é policial, segundo as autoridades. Caso aconteceu em uma escola de Canton, no Michigan, nesta segunda-feira (28).
articles.body:
IMAGEM ILUSTRATIVA: Pistola — Foto: Pixabay

Uma criança pequena levou uma arma carregada para uma creche no estado de Michigan, nos Estados Unidos , nesta segunda-feira (28). Segundo as autoridades, a criança chegou a retirar a pistola de dentro de uma mochila. Um dos pais foi detido.

O caso aconteceu na cidade de Canton. As autoridades afirmaram que um dos pais da criança trabalha como policial na região. A polícia não informou se o responsável detido é o policial nem detalhou se é o pai ou a mãe da criança.

Segundo o chefe da polícia local, Joseph Bialy, funcionários da creche perceberam que a criança estava com a arma e agiram rapidamente. A polícia foi chamada e apreendeu a pistola. Ninguém ficou ferido.

Bialy afirmou que a ação foi registrada por câmeras de monitoramento interno. As imagens não foram divulgadas.

"É chocante ver uma criança tão pequena manuseando uma arma de fogo", disse Bialy.

A polícia ainda investiga como a arma foi parar na mochila da criança. Segundo Bialy, aparentemente, a pistola apreendida não é uma arma usada pela corporação.

A creche informou à polícia que vai reforçar os protocolos de segurança e passar a fazer buscas nas mochilas das crianças. Segundo Bialy, os funcionários já tinham procedimentos de segurança.

Na Base Aérea, em Brasília, Lula sancionou projeto que amplia a profissionalização do futebol feminino. Na sequência, seguiu para Belém.

No Hospital São João de Deus, o presidente acompanhou a primeira cirurgia robótica oncológica feita pelo SUS na Amazônia. A visita não foi aberta à imprensa. Na saída, recebeu uma camisa em homenagem ao Círio de Nazaré, entregue pela governadora Hana Ghassan, do MDB, candidata à reeleição, e disse que pretende investir mais no tratamento de câncer pelo SUS:

“Hoje, no tratamento de câncer, a nossa decisão é: que entre detectar o câncer e começar o tratamento seja no máximo 30 dias. Ninguém vai morrer esperando. A gente está criando centros em todas as cidades com mais de 250 mil habitantes".

articles.title: Ponte cai durante passagem de caminhão com bois e 8 animais morrem | G1
articles.standfirst: Estrutura sobre o rio Mimoso desabou nesta segunda-feira (28); motorista não ficou ferido e prefeitura prevê construção de uma nova ponte em 2027.
articles.summary: Estrutura sobre o rio Mimoso desabou nesta segunda-feira (28); motorista não ficou ferido e prefeitura prevê construção de uma nova ponte em 2027.
articles.body:
Uma ponte sobre o rio Mimoso, em Bonito , caiu na manhã desta segunda-feira (28), enquanto um caminhão carregado com bois passava pelo trecho. Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, dos 21 animais que estavam no veículo, oito morreram. O motorista não ficou ferido. Veja o vídeo acima.

Imagens feitas após o acidente mostram o caminhão no local e a estrutura destruída. Segundo o subtenente Euro, do Corpo de Bombeiros, o atendimento à ocorrência durou cerca de 1h30. Para retirar os animais, foi necessário cortar parte da gaiola do caminhão.

De acordo com o bombeiro, alguns animais morreram afogados após ficarem presos sob outros bois. O caminhoneiro e o dono da carga prestaram apoio durante o atendimento.

De acordo com o prefeito de Bonito, Josmail Rodrigues, a estrada tem pouco movimento e a estrutura foi inaugurada em 2022.

Segundo ele, a ponte já apresentava restrição para a passagem de caminhões pesados e tinha previsão de revisão. Ele também afirmou que a madeira usada na construção era de baixa qualidade.

Ainda segundo o prefeito, uma nova ponte será construída no local, mas a previsão é que a obra ocorra apenas em 2027. A data ainda não foi definida, pois o projeto precisa passar por processo de licitação, que, segundo ele, é demorado.

articles.title: Marconi Perillo promete salário mínimo de R$ 2.200 em Goiás | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato prometeu criar uma ajuda para quem recebe apenas um salário mínimo com carteira assinada. Ao lado de apoiadores, aliados políticos e de assessores, o candidato do PSDB participou de uma caminhada.
articles.summary: Marconi Perillo propõe criar um salário mínimo regional em Goiás para complementar a renda de quem trabalha com carteira assinada e recebe o piso nacional.
articles.body:
O candidato ao governo de Goiás, Marconi Perillo ( PSDB ), cumpriu agenda em Morrinhos , no sul do estado nesta segunda-feira (28), e prometeu criar uma ajuda para quem recebe apenas um salário mínimo com carteira assinada. Marconi Perillo apresentou propostas do plano de governo, entre elas estão o compromisso sobre política social.

"Nós vamos criar o salário mínimo regional, o salário mínimo de Goiás, no valor de 2.200 para todas as famílias que tiverem um membro com salário mínimo, com carteira assinada. Ao invés da gente dar bolsas, nós vamos estimular a carteira assinada", disse.

Marconi pretende também dar autonomia às pessoas por meio de oportunidades de qualificação, emprego, empreendedorismo e geração de renda. O candidato defende uma política social integrada para que o Estado acompanhe o cidadão em várias áreas, como qualificação profissional, habitação e proteção de direitos.

"A pessoa tem um trabalho efetivo, está fichado, se ganha um salário mínimo o governo complementa a renda para que nenhuma família de Goiás possa passar necessidades. Mas o estímulo nosso vai ser para a produtividade e para o trabalho ativo", afirmou.

Ao lado de apoiadores, aliados políticos e de assessores, o candidato do PSDB participou de uma caminhada por uma das principais avenidas da cidade, onde cumprimentou eleitores e comerciantes. Marconi prometeu retomar e atualizar o Renda Cidadã, criado na gestão em que ele foi governador.

articles.summary: Animal foi flagrado praticamente imóvel na água após se alimentar; moradores chegaram a pensar que a cobra estivesse morta, mas perceberam que ela fazia a digestão.
articles.body:
Com os termômetros “beirando” os 40 °C, um banho no Córrego Amaralina, em Coxim , era uma boa pedida. Foi exatamente o que fizeram o instalador de piscinas Edilson Aparecido, de 33 anos, e a família. Mas, ao chegarem ao local, no domingo (27), eles encontraram muito mais do que sombra e água fresca.

Uma sucuri com a barriga cheia e aparentemente com cerca de cinco metros de comprimento surpreendeu os moradores e rendeu imagens impressionantes. Veja no vídeo acima.

⚠️ Especialistas alertam que não se deve aproximar nem incomodar uma sucuri, principalmente depois que ela se alimenta. A digestão pode levar semanas e, caso a cobra se sinta ameaçada, pode regurgitar a presa. Esse processo pode provocar complicações e até levar o animal à morte. A orientação é manter distância e não tentar tocar na serpente.

Edilson conta que o córrego onde fez as imagens fica a cerca de 20 km do perímetro urbano de Coxim, no sentido do Pantanal.

“Fomos tomar um banho: eu, minha esposa, meus filhos, minha prima, o esposo dela e ainda tinha um outro pessoal lá. Foram eles que viram e avisaram a gente. Aí eu fui lá e gravei o vídeo”, explica o morador.

O vídeo mostra a sucuri com um grande volume na barriga, parada no curso d’água e observando a aproximação dos banhistas. O tamanho do animal foi o que mais impressionou.

“Ela deveria ter mais ou menos uns cinco metros de comprimento”, estima Edilson.

Como a serpente estava praticamente imóvel, num primeiro momento, os banhistas chegaram a pensar que ela estivesse morta. Logo, porém, perceberam que a sucuri estava viva e havia acabado de se alimentar.

“O pessoal que estava lá se assustou, mas a gente, que já está acostumado com fazenda e já tinha visto, não se assustou. Quando a gente chegou lá e viu que ela estava viva, a gente deixou ela quieta, né? Porque ela está fazendo digestão”, comenta Edilson.

Sucuri de barriga cheia em rio de MS. — Foto: Reprodução.

As imagens também impressionam porque ajudam a dimensionar algumas das adaptações naturais do corpo da espécie. A sucuri possui uma mandíbula bastante flexível, capaz de ampliar consideravelmente a abertura da boca.

A espécie também tem pele elástica e costelas móveis, características que permitem ao animal engolir presas de grande porte como as capivaras.

A sucuri é uma serpente da família Boidae, pertencente ao gênero Eunectes, com distribuição geográfica restrita à América do Sul. Apesar de não ser ágil em ambiente terrestre, a espécie é muito eficiente dentro d’água e pode permanecer até 30 minutos sem respirar.

articles.title: Empresário de 39 anos morre em acidente na RJ-148, entre Nova Friburgo | G1
articles.standfirst: Thiago da Silva Rodrigues morreu no local após o carro capotar em uma curva da rodovia. Corpo foi sepultado na noite desta segunda (28). Polícia investiga o acidente; trecho é alvo de reclamações.
articles.summary: Thiago da Silva Rodrigues morreu no local após o carro capotar. Corpo foi sepultado na noite desta segunda (28). Polícia investiga o acidente; trecho é alvo de reclamações.
articles.body:
O empresário Thiago da Silva Rodrigues, de 39 anos, morreu após acidente na RJ-148, entre Nova Friburgo e Sumidouro — Foto: Reprodução redes sociais

Um empresário de 39 anos morreu em um acidente na RJ-148, rodovia que liga Nova Friburgo a Sumidouro , na Região Serrana do Rio. O acidente aconteceu na noite de domingo (27), por volta das 19h.

A vítima foi identificada como Thiago da Silva Rodrigues, que teve o corpo sepultado na noite desta segunda-feira (28), no Memorial. Ele conduzia um carro de passeio quando sofreu o acidente em uma curva da rodovia, na região de Sumidouro.

Segundo testemunhas, Thiago perdeu o controle do veículo durante uma ultrapassagem. O carro teria atingido uma pedra depois do meio-fio e capotado. Ele morreu ainda no local, antes da chegada das equipes de socorro do Corpo de Bombeiros.

As circunstâncias do acidente são investigadas pela polícia. Até a última atualização desta reportagem, não há confirmação de que as condições da RJ-148 tenham contribuído para a batida.

Thiago era empresário e sócio de uma loja de venda de veículos em Riograndina, distrito de Nova Friburgo que também é cortado pela RJ-148.

articles.title: Gone in 90 seconds: an ‘invisibilized’ ICE is arresting more people than ever
articles.summary: After public backlash, the Trump administration changed its tactics from ‘siege’ to ‘soft feet’. Now, ICE is everywhere
articles.body:
Those who lived through it describe the ICE raids as a "siege" or an "occupation".

At the height of the raids last year, agents in armored military vehicles rolled through residential neighborhoods. Masked agents patrolled public parks and stationed themselves outside elementary schools; squadrons of Immigration and Customs Enforcement ( ICE ) agents snatched pedestrians off the streets.

Then, officers killed two US citizens during an ICE "blitz" on Minneapolis. After a public backlash, the Trump administration said it would try a new approach.

"I learned that maybe we could use a little bit of a softer touch," Donald Trump said in February. He chose a new secretary of homeland security, Markwayne Mullin, who promised to cut the flash and fanfare. "My goal in six months is that we're not in the lead story every single day," he said at his Senate confirmation hearing in March.

Six months on, that's what his agency has delivered.

Now ICE is anywhere and everywhere, embedded in all corners of everyday life.

A Cuban man in Miami who stepped outside his house to take out the trash was detained moments after he had dropped the garbage bag into the bin. An Ecuadorian father was arrested in Danbury, Connecticut, just after seeing his six-year-old son on to the school bus. People have been arrested while pumping gas, leaving behind their empty cars. They are arrested on their way to work, or on their way home.

Y, a Venezuelan native, was stopped at the Phoenix Sky Harbor airport by immigration officers whom he said wouldn't tell him why he was being arrested, or accept proof of a judicial order expressly prohibiting deportation to his home country. Four days later, he was on an airplane departing to Venezuela. Just before takeoff, he was deboarded – ICE officers admitted they may have made a mistake.

Though agents appear to be moving with more stealth than they were before, ICE arrests are still, often, violent. Glimpses of that violence are – despite Mullin's initial intentions – still making national headlines.

Last week, an ICE agent shot Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez in Austin, Texas. The Venezuelan asylum seeker, who had received a deportation order after missing a letter to appear in immigration court, was discharged from a local hospital with a bullet still lodged near his spine and then taken to ICE detention. That same day, in Grand Rapids, Michigan, a Guatemalan man died in a fiery crash while fleeing federal immigration agents.

Still, for every arrest that breaks through into public view, countless others happen quickly, before anyone can notice. "The detentions are happening in a flash – we're talking, like, 90 seconds from the time ICE shows up to that person being driven away," Willis said. "And often they are moving very quietly, with very soft feet."

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), the US government agency that oversees ICE , declined to comment on how its tactics had changed. "DHS will not disclose or discuss law enforcement operations, strategy or tactics," said Chandler Rebel, a spokesperson for the agency. But Rebel confirmed the agency's focus on airports, noting the DHS was "working diligently to ensure that aliens in our country illegally can no longer fly unless it is out of our country to self-deport".

Bolstered by $75bn in funding from Congress, the Department of Homeland Security – the US government agency that oversees ICE – has more than doubled its workforce this year to more than 22,000 officers and staff. It has also vastly expanded its capacity by working with local police, sheriffs, highway patrol and even fish and wildlife agents. As of 15 September, ICE had signed more than 2,500 287(g) agreements .

ICE is now detaining more immigrants than ever before.

An expanded dragnet fueled by police partnerships

"The administration is able to essentially hide a multiplied ICE force not only in unmarked cars, and not only behind masks, but also within local law enforcement through the 287(g) program," said Willis. "I call it the invisibilizing of immigration enforcement."

Operations that now originate with local police are taking place across the country.

At the El Corralón bar in Memphis on 29 August, an operation that began as a police raid targeting illegal gambling and drugs turned into one of the largest sweeps of undocumented immigrants in Tennessee – 120 people were detained. Immigration agents worked with state law enforcement to execute search warrants at the bar related to drugs and gambling, and targeting the bar's owner. But then, at 1am that night, more than a dozen agents walked into the bar, shut off the music, instructed everyone to gather on the dancefloor and asked them one by one if they had legal status, according to witnesses .

A spokesperson for the DHS said partnerships with law enforcement agencies were key to the agency's immigration enforcement. "We have had tremendous success when local law enforcement works together with us," said Rebel.

Lawyers across the US said they worried that local law enforcement officials are not adequately aware of the nuances of immigration policy. "People are getting detained if they don't have their green card on them. They're getting stopped even if they have legal status," said Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, an immigration attorney based in Austin.

Last month, her client Brian José Morales García, 25, was deported to Mexico despite repeatedly telling officers that he was a US citizen, born in Denver.

Morales García was on his way to work as an air-conditioning installation tech, riding with his boss, when officers from the Gillespie county sheriff's department and the Texas department of public safety (DPS) pulled them over. Both law enforcement agencies were working with ICE. Morales García told the officers that he had his birth certificate and social security card at home, but they didn't believe him. Days later, he was deported to Mexico.

Eventually, the federal government reached an agreement with Morales García's lawyers to let him back into the country, after Lincoln-Goldfinch submitted documents proving his citizenship.

"We're seeing a lot of racial profiling," she said. Local law enforcement appear to be especially active in Hispanic neighborhoods , she said, or in areas where Latino construction workers gather.

"They might have their sights set on a big job site, in some neighborhood under construction, and just slowly patrol that site and just take people in day after day until nobody's going to work there any more," she said.

The Trump administration has also relentlessly reshaped immigration policies and bent the country's vast bureaucracy to advance its mass-deportation agenda and boost arrest numbers.

"In order to sustain those numbers, they have to create more categories of people who can be subject to detention," said Willis. "They do this by creating new pathways to deportation."

In recent months, the supreme court cleared the way for the administration to end temporary humanitarian protections for 350,000 Haitians and Syrians in the US and made it easier to end protections for a total of about 1.3 million immigrants from a number of countries designated for temporary protected status (TPS). Currently, about 170,000 Salvadorians living in the US are anxiously waiting for the administration to announce whether it will renew or axe the same protections for them.

At the same time, the administration unrolled a new tactic of scheduling "mega-master" hearings – mass hearings in immigration courts, scheduled at the last minute so that many people do not know to, or are unable to, attend their mandatory court appointments. The no-shows are then ordered removed from the country in absentia, making them immediately subject to arrest and deportation.

After attorneys began reporting such hearings in May, judges issued 53,808 removal orders in absentia in June – a 55% increase. More than 13,000 of those removal orders followed mass hearings with a hundred or more people, according to researchers Joseph Gunther and Brandon Marrow, who created the site bklg.org to track and analyze procedural immigration data.

In the coming weeks, the Trump administration is also expected to revoke the business and tourism visas of up to 200,000 foreigners. It has implemented a rule allowing officials to block people from becoming lawful permanent residents if they or certain relatives use public benefits such as Medicaid, food stamps or even student financial aid.

It is also increasingly pursuing "third-country" deportation agreements, so it can arrest and remove immigrants who were previously immune to removal because a judge had deemed that they would face torture or persecution if they were returned to their home countries. Now, more than 23,000 people over the last year have been expelled to countries where they have never been and where they have no ties. Some of these deportations are to countries with civil unrest, political instability, armed conflict and known human rights abuses.

There are constantly shifting rules about who can or cannot be detained or deported, and for how long. And there are constantly shifting norms on who will be detained or deported.

On one day, a client might go to an ICE check-in and leave without incident, Willis said. The next day, a different client with the same immigration status might be detained. "It makes it very hard to counsel people," Willis said. "It's very hard to prepare people for what they can expect."

Not everyone who is arrested is immediately deportable – many people have pending immigration cases, or legal status. Indeed, there is a wide gulf between the number of people ICE is detaining each month, and the number of people who are deported.

Many of the people who are arrested languish in detention for months. Others – even those who may have a good chance of gaining asylum or another legal status – choose to accept voluntary deportation rather than wait months or years for their immigration case to process.

Federal circuit courts are currently split on whether immigrants who came to the US without lawful admission, including many asylum seekers, can be detained indefinitely without access to bond hearings. In some states, including Texas, the prospect of spending years inside a detention center can wear on immigrants.

"Almost every single detained parent that I talk to has been pressured into signing a voluntary deportation," said Lincoln-Goldfinch. "Because they are told that if they sign, they get to go home and they can choose what happens to their kids."

The Guardian is not using full names in some instances to protect sources' privacy and safety

The data for this story is based on the rolling seven-day average arrest figures from the Deportation Data Project , an effort led by a team of academics and lawyers at the University of California, Berkeley and the University of California, Los Angeles tracking immigration enforcement using government data. The Guardian followed the Deportation Data Project's methodology for simplifying the apprehension methods listed by ICE in the group's data. Immigration enforcement in communities are labeled as "at large arrests", and include apprehension methods labeled "non-custodial arrest", "located", "probation and parole" and "worksite enforcement". Transfers from jail or prison are "custodial arrests", from apprehension methods labeled "CAP local incarceration", "CAP federal incarceration", "CAP state incarceration" and "custodial arrest". Local police under 287(g) program arrests are from the apprehension method labeled "287(g) program". The Guardian measured the date of the new approach from 24 March 2026, the day that Markwayne Mullin was confirmed as secretary of the DHS.

articles.title: SG: Government to tighten rules to block under-18 accounts on social media platforms
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Agreeing with Supreme Court, Centre on Monday said it would soon insert a provision in the Information and Technology Intermediary Rules to
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Agreeing with Supreme Court, Centre on Monday said it would soon insert a provision in the Information and Technology Intermediary Rules to prevent social media intermediaries from allowing children under 18 years of age to open social media accounts, reports Dhananjay Mahapatra.Agreeing with the bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana as well as petitioner NGO 'Just Rights for Children Alliance' counsel H S Phoolka, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said the agreements entered into by intermediaries and minors were void contracts and these must be prevented.Membership of educational websites can be taken through consent of parents," solicitor general Tushar Mehta said, adding that Centre would step in to make it a statutory obligation for intermediaries not to allow minors to have social media accounts.Justice Bagchi said, "They have registered under the laws of US and imported into Indian digital space the restrictions which are applicable in US (on minors' opening accounts on social media platforms), which is impermissible under Indian law."When Mehta said "we will have to control intermediaries", the bench responded, "Our request to you - will Centre pass some directions under Intermediary Rules that they should fashion their software or platform in conformity with Indian laws?"The SG said, "They will have to conform to Indian laws and there is no doubt about it. Something can be done, something should be done and something will be done." Justice Bagchi said, "They must restrict, at least in registering membership, to a minimum threshold of 18 years." The SG agreed and said it must now be inserted in some law or rules to make intermediaries compliant with Indian laws.Senior advocate Phoolka said govt had certain guidelines on this issue, which needed enforcement. The SG said it must now be enforced through a statute. CJI Kant said it must be through a statutory mechanism as the SG said and asked govt to consider it and get back with a response.The NGO complained that "absence of an effective and uniform mechanism giving practical effect to such statutory incapacity in the digital environment exposes children to foreseeable risks, including online grooming, sexual exploitation, trafficking, behavioural profiling, misuse of personal data, cyberbullying, exposure to age-inappropriate content."Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Candace Owens faces growing pressure as family voices ‘safety’ fears amid Charlie Kirk controversy and lawsuits
articles.summary: Candace Owens is facing growing concern from people close to her as she continues to promote theories about Charlie Kirk’s killing and fights two
articles.body: Candace Owens is facing growing concern from people close to her as she continues to promote theories about Charlie Kirk’s killing and fights two defamation cases. A family member told the Daily Mail, “I pray every day for her safety,” and said, “I would like for her to get fully out of it. Don’t talk anymore. Just disappear.” Owens has rejected speculation that her June trip to Russia was linked to plans to leave the US. Her legal troubles include a lawsuit from Kirk’s former security chief Brian Harpole and another from Emmanuel and Brigitte Macron.Candace Owens’ Charlie Kirk claims bring family and security concernsOwens recently devoted three episodes of her YouTube show to claims about Kirk’s death, including the suggestion that a “decoy” was used and that Kirk was not shot. The episodes drew about 3.9 million views combined, while her channel has passed six million subscribers.She had also spent earlier episodes discussing Kirk’s widow, Erika Kirk, and making claims that have not been supported by evidence. The attention has added to worries among people around Owens. Her former security team said protecting her became “more challenging” as her public comments became more provocative.Her comments about Kirk have also moved into the courts. Brian Harpole, who served as Kirk’s former head of security, filed a federal defamation case against Owens in Tennessee in April 2026. Court records show the case is active in the U.S. District Court in Tennessee as of June 2026. Harpole alleges that Owens linked him to a conspiracy surrounding Kirk’s death. Owens has disputed the claims.Candace Owens’ Russia trip and ongoing legal fightsOwens’ June trip to Russia has become another point of discussion. Reuters reported that she attended the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum, where she was scheduled to speak about parenting and careers. The Daily Mail said one person who had worked with Kirk and other conservative figures viewed the trip as possible preparation for protecting Owens’ assets if she loses her lawsuits. The source stressed that she may not have made a final decision.Owens rejected the idea that she plans to move to Russia, calling it a “lie” and one of several “crazy stories.”Her other major legal fight is with French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife, Brigitte Macron. They accuse Owens of defamation over claims she has made about Brigitte Macron. The case is still ongoing, according to court-related reporting.Owens has continued defending her public work. “I would rather be completely isolated and speak the absolute truth than sit at the table of compromise,” she said last year.Her career has changed sharply since she began as a progressive commentator. Charlie Kirk hired her at Turning Point USA in 2017, and she later joined The Daily Wire before leaving in 2024. Since then, she has built her own media business and continued speaking to a large online audience, even as former allies and family members have raised concerns about her direction.You use AI every day. articles.title: UAE confirms Netanyahu’s secret visit, says talks focused on Iran, bilateral ties
articles.summary: The United Arab Emirates on Monday confirmed that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited the Gulf country on Sunday, saying his meeting with
articles.body: The United Arab Emirates on Monday confirmed that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited the Gulf country on Sunday, saying his meeting with UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan focused on bilateral relations. Israeli officials, meanwhile, said the talks also focused on Iran.The UAE’s state news agency WAM reported that Sheikh Mohamed and Netanyahu discussed bilateral relations during the visit. It was the first official confirmation from Abu Dhabi of Netanyahu’s trip.Netanyahu’s office said the prime minister had travelled to the UAE at the invitation of Sheikh Mohamed. The visit “focused on strengthening relations between the two countries and on regional challenges”, his office said.Three senior Israeli officials told Reuters that the meeting lasted six hours and focused on Iran, according to the report. Earlier accounts had described the meeting as lasting about an hour.The visit was first reported by Israel’s Channel 12 television station. Two people briefed on the trip confirmed that Netanyahu met Sheikh Mohamed on Sunday.One person familiar with the meeting told news agency AP that Netanyahu asked the Emirati president to deny a recent report in Haaretz alleging that Sheikh Mohamed had warned Israel about a looming Hamas attack shortly before the October 7, 2023, assault. Netanyahu’s office had previously denied the Haaretz report.The UAE had earlier denied a meeting between the two leaders after Netanyahu’s office said in May that he had “secretly visited” the country. A source familiar with that meeting said at the time that Netanyahu and Sheikh Mohamed met in Al-Ain on March 26.Late Monday, the UAE said the latest meeting covered bilateral relations “and ways to strengthen and develop them”. Netanyahu’s office said it focused “solely on strengthening relations” and denied that he asked Sheikh Mohamed to address the Haaretz report.Netanyahu’s office also said the Shin Bet had filed a complaint against Channel 12, alleging a violation of censorship rules over its report before Netanyahu returned to Israel. The latest visit is expected to keep Iran and regional security high on the agenda of UAE-Israel engagement.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: SC to CBSE: Exempt Class VI from 3-language education policy this year
articles.summary: New Delhi: Supreme Court on Monday ordered CBSE to exempt Class VI students from the three-language policy, under which they have to choose two Indian
articles.body: New Delhi: Supreme Court on Monday ordered CBSE to exempt Class VI students from the three-language policy, under which they have to choose two Indian languages. A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, which had requested CBSE to reconsider its decision to implement the policy from this year, ordered that the policy would now be implemented for Class VI students from the next academic year.For CBSE, solicitor general Tushar Mehta said textbooks and logistics for implementation of the policy have been taken care of and that out of 28,819 schools, 98.8% have already complied with the new policy. The bench said the figure of 1.2% of schools not implementing it meant around 300 of them, which is a large number.Didn't students study online during Covid?When one counsel said the study material is available only through digital textbooks and online mode, causing students difficulties, Justice Mohana asked, "Did the students not study during Covid pandemic when learning was through online mode? Every child, even from a house help's house, had a phone. Have a better reason."Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati said there will be no pass or fail under the three-language policy. On two issues - validity of the policy and whether English should be treated as foreign language - the bench said these would be decided after six weeks.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: The BJP on Monday accused the opposition parties of trying to vitiate the country's atmosphere and spread chaos amid their protest against the Election Commission, alleging that the sole agenda of netas like Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and Arvind Kejriwal was to "grab power" by any means."Their toolkit mindset is at work: Level allegations, vitiate the country's atmosphere and run away," Union health and family welfare minister J P Nadda said, claiming that the EC's statement following a joint meeting of its three members had exposed the opposition's fabricated charge against the poll body and govt. "Rahul Gandhi should realise that repeating a lie a hundred times cannot make it true," he said.Opposition parties have cited an Indian Express report, which suggested that CEC Gyanesh Kumar was acting unilaterally over the implementation of SIR as it highlighted written objections from two election commissioners, to step up their attack on the commission and have demanded Kumar's resignation.BJP has seized on the EC's statement on Saturday, which said all SIR related decisions were unanimous while announcing measures to address some of the issues, to assert that it has exposed the "falsehood" of the opposition's campaign.Nadda said the people of the country had fully understood the double standards and the negative politics of the opposition. articles.title: Coast Guard saves sinking tanker with 23 crew off Odisha coast

articles.body: NEW DELHI: In an operation to avert a major disaster at sea, Indian Coast Guard Sunday rescued a foreign-flagged tanker carrying 23 crew members and 9,000 tonnes of palm oil after its main engine failed, ballast tanks began flooding and the vessel was dangerously tilted off Odisha coast, reports Surendra Singh.The Belize-flagged MT Seagull 9 sent out a distress call around 7.30am Sunday, when it was 37 nautical miles east-southeast of Paradip. Following a critical distress call from MT Seagull 9 off Paradip, ICGS Vishwast launched a swift & decisive operation to rescue the unstable chemical tanker carrying 9,000 MT palm oil & 23 crew members." articles.title: Pentagon breach exposed sensitive data on nearly 3 million people
articles.summary: The breach included Social Security numbers and details about jobs people held.
articles.body:
A breach of the Pentagon's sprawling personnel database exposed sensitive information belonging to a massive swath of military personnel, including Social Security numbers and details about the jobs they held, according to a U.S. defense official.

The breach affected 2.76 million living people and another 294,000 who are deceased, the official said. The scope and sensitivity of the exposed information could raise national security concerns, particularly because the files included details about the jobs performed by military and civilian personnel.

"A Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC) information system experienced unauthorized access of personally identifiable information by a small number of unauthorized users between October 2025 and July 2026. Upon discovery, DMDC immediately remediated the vulnerability," the official said.

The Defense Manpower Data Center serves as one of the Pentagon's main repositories for personnel records, holding information on active-duty and reserve troops, civilian employees, contractors, retirees, veterans and military family members.

The agency maintains more than 60 million personnel records. Military Times first reported the breach last week.

The unauthorized access stretched from October 2025 until July, when DMDC discovered the vulnerability and patched the affected system, according to the defense official, adding there's no evidence yet that any of the exposed data has been misused.

Defense officials said they have found no evidence so far that the exposed information has been misused and are offering identity protection and credit monitoring resources.

The news of the Pentagon breach comes as the FBI sent a notice to employees on Friday outlining their response to a breach of its jobs portal FBIJobs.gov .

An threat actor said it would publish data including FBI employees' names, home address, personal and work contact information, Social Security numbers, date of birth and emergency contact information, sources told ABC News, and the bureau is operating as if every FBI employee's personal information was compromised.

But in a statement to the New York Times and 404 Media on Monday, the hacking group shinyhunters claimed it won't release the data as it previously said it would.

"Since the very beginning of this event we have unequivocally and assiduously emphasised this is NOT extortion, this is NOT ransom, this is NOT financially motivated," the statement said. "This was all a marketing campaign to protect our business and actively combat disinformation. If we made this statement normally then this much attention to our words and intentions would've never been this widespread."

ABC News has not independently verified the group's claims.

Employees who were impacted have also begun to be notified, and the FBI said that the impacted system -- FBIJobs.gov -- was unclassified.

The FBI also issued a warning for those who might be impacted, advising them to maintain situational awareness and to not answer suspicious calls. There will also be internal briefings for employees who have been impacted.

It also says, according to the warning described to ABC News, that employees should not talk to the media and if the media is "trespassing," employees should call 911.

articles.title: AAP donations fall 68%, BJD reports zero contributions
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party's receipts from contributions in 2025-26 fell to Rs 12.1 crore, which is less than one-third of its Rs 38.1 crore inflow
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party's receipts from contributions in 2025-26 fell to Rs 12.1 crore, which is less than one-third of its Rs 38.1 crore inflow through this route in 2024-25. Of this, Rs 10 crore, or 83% of its total donations, came from Prudent Electoral Trust and Trident Group founded by Rajya Sabha MP Rajendra Gupta, who switched loyalties from AAP to BJP earlier this year.AAP is the only party that declares all donation receipts and not just those above Rs 20,000 as required by the law. According to its latest contribution report filed with Election Commission (EC), both Prudent and Trident contributed Rs 5 crore each to AAP; in 2024-25, Prudent had donated Rs 16.4 crore to the party.Among regional parties, TDP, which is in office in Andhra Pradesh since 2024, declared its donation receipts at Rs 58.3 crore, though this is less than the Rs 83 crore contributions it had reported the previous year. Prudent contributed over 77% of TDP's total receipts through six donations in 2025-26. In 2024-25 too, Prudent was TDP's biggest donor, having contributed Rs 40 crore in all.YSR Congress Party, the main opposition party in Andhra Pradesh, received a total of Rs 24.3 crore in donations in 2025-26, though this figure is way less than its Rs 140 crore inflow in 2024-25.BRS, which was voted out of office by Congress in Telangana in 2023, declared its total contributions in 2025-26 at Rs 16.4 crore, up from Rs 15.1 crore in 2024-25. The 2025-26 contribution report for Biju Janata Dal (BJD), which was defeated in Odisha in 2024, records nil donations, as against Rs 60 crore declared in 2024-25.Part of AAP's donations in the last fiscal came from its MLAs, including former Delhi CMs Arvind Kejriwal (Rs 30,000) and Atishi Marlena (Rs 42,000).Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Iran’s Araghchi meets Qatari mediators as US calls for nuclear talks
articles.summary: Tehran awaits reply on Hormuz plan as a US official says there will be no deal unless nuclear issues are addressed.
articles.body:
Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has met with Qatari mediators in New York to discuss a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while a United States official said there would be no agreement to end the war unless Tehran’s nuclear programme is addressed.

Araghchi told Iranian state media on Monday that the Qatari mediators would carry the ideas discussed at the meeting to the US and that he hoped to receive Washington’s final response by Tuesday.

“We talked about ideas and how to find solutions to fulfil Iran’s conditions and how to implement those conditions,” he said. “They had some ideas, and we had a discussion that they will also present to the American side.”

Asked whether he would stay in New York to await the reply, Araghchi said he would fly to Tehran within hours.

“Whenever the Qataris have a response, they know how to get it to us,” he said.

He described the meetings as part of an existing exchange of messages through Qatari and Pakistani mediators, which he said had taken on “a more serious form” since Iran submitted its proposal.

The Iranian plan , announced on Friday at the United Nations General Assembly in New York City, calls on the US to release frozen Iranian funds, lift sanctions and end its naval blockade of Iranian ports. Araghchi said those steps could be completed within four or five days, allowing the strait to reopen and negotiations on a final agreement, including on Iran’s nuclear programme, to begin by the seventh day.

US President Donald Trump, however, rejected the proposal on Saturday, calling it “unacceptable”.

The US official, who spoke to Al Jazeera, said indirect discussions were continuing.

The talks were “positive and constructive”, the official said, but stressed there would be no agreement unless Iran’s nuclear programme is addressed. The official said Trump is willing to relieve sanctions and release Iran’s frozen funds in exchange for progress on nuclear issues.

“Iran has indicated they are flexible on the nuclear issues, but the sides still remain apart on the timing of the commitments and who takes which steps first,” the official said.

The official also expressed scepticism of Iran, saying it had broken the memorandum of understanding signed in June by firing on commercial vessels. Tehran denies the accusation and says it was Washington that broke its commitments by failing to halt Israel’s attacks on Lebanon and by seeking to establish alternate shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran had closed the strait, which handled roughly 20 percent of the world’s oil and gas supplies before the war, shortly after the US and Israel launched their offensive on February 28. Iranian attacks on vessels since have sharply curtailed shipping, and oil prices have risen above $100 a barrel.

Even so, crude exports from major Middle East producers rebounded in September to 12.8 million barrels per day, their highest level since the war began, the Reuters news agency reported, citing data from the maritime intelligence firm Kpler.

That is still well below the 18.8 million bpd exported in February.

Some ships have used the US military-supervised route hugging the coast of Oman, travelling at night with tracking systems off and offloading oil to tankers outside the strait. Admiral Brad Cooper, the head of US Central Command, said on Saturday that American forces had assisted 2,000 transits and more than 1 billion barrels of oil in recent months.

The US has also imposed a blockade on Iranian ports and threatened secondary sanctions against airports and companies that do business with Iranian airlines. The United Arab Emirates, Iraq and Oman have already cancelled related flights.

Speaking to reporters on Monday, Trump said US officials had also spoken with mediators but insisted that Washington would prevail.

“We’re going to win,” he said. “It’s going to go pretty quickly.” He added that gas prices would fall once the US won the war.

In Tehran, officials struck a defiant tone.

Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, in a message marking the Iran-Iraq War and Israel’s killing of Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah in 2024, said that the days of foreign domination were over.

“Having suffered painful blows from our valiant combatants and the guardians of the Strait of Hormuz, they [the enemy] dare not venture beyond the Arabian Sea,” Khamenei said in the message carried by Iranian media.

“Whenever they have risked doing so, they have only inflicted harm upon themselves, and the time is fast approaching when the Arabian Sea, too, will be cleared of their presence.”

Major-General Ali Abdollahi, the armed forces chief of staff, meanwhile, warned that Iran and allied forces would deliver a “decisive and devastating response” to any threat against the country.

Rear Admiral Habibollah Sayyari insisted that the Strait of Hormuz remains closed and said Iranian forces were ready to prevent enemy forces from entering the country.

articles.title: Britain’s PM is on a ‘Burnham bounce.’ When will he fall to earth?
articles.summary: The problems which plagued Andy Burnham’s predecessor, including over immigration, the souring of the economy and rising geopolitical tensions, linger on.
articles.body: Some have dubbed it the “Burnham bounce.” That is, the surge in public support for the UK’s governing Labour Party after the former mayor of Manchester Andy Burnham took to the helm this summer as the country’s seventh prime minister in a decade. But the problems which plagued Burnham’s predecessor, including over immigration, the souring of the economy amid the Iran war and rising geopolitical tensions, linger – and cannot be fixed by optimism alone. This week, Burnham is under intense pressure to demonstrate he has a solution to such issues at the first Labour Party conference of his premiership, all while the hard-right Reform UK party closely tails Labour in the polls. So, what are the key hurdles that Burnham must overcome? Squeezed by the right and left Despite facing a drumbeat of allegations about its party finances in recent months, Nigel Farage’s Reform UK is only narrowly behind Labour in the polls – something Farage pointed to when Burnham recently ruled out an early general election. “It’s obvious that Andy Burnham doesn’t want talk of a General Election overshadowing Labour’s conference,” Farage posted on X Friday. “Reform are ready for an election whenever it is called.” Reform has lost some buoyancy following a string of damning financial scandals, the latest of which prompted a criminal investigation into party donations. Reform denies any wrongdoing and says it will “cooperate fully with the investigation.” But the populist, anti-migrant party – which won big in England’s local elections earlier this year – clearly poses a threat to Burnham, particularly as anti-immigrant sentiments are bubbling to the surface in some parts of the country. Earlier this month, major anti-migration protests swept along parts of Britain’s coastline with hundreds of balaclava-wearing demonstrators blocking roads and clashing with police, scenes which Burnham called “unacceptable.” “This is not something we have seen in this country before,” he told the BBC on Sunday, while accepting that “there are real worries about immigration in all parts of country.” Meanwhile, the prime minister is having to claw back progressives who defected to the Green Party under Starmer, as left-wing factions sought pastures new over Labour’s stance on issues like net zero and the Gaza conflict. The threat posed by the Greens will be tested next week when the party’s leader, Zack Polanski, contests an election to become the next Member of Parliament (MP) in London’s Holborn and St Pancras constituency – Starmer’s former seat for over a decade. The economy During his first weeks as prime minister, Burnham announced a raft of policies targeting Britain’s economic woes, aiming to ease the pressure on cash-strapped households. One policy was the reduction of bus fares in England, outside of London, to a maximum of £2 (about $2.60). He also announced plans to cut business rates bills for pubs and music venues, and touted other tax cuts for household electricity bills. Such commitments have been cast as small fry by some challengers. “I find myself asking, is that it?” Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch said in July. And the pledges Burnham set out, including building more social housing and bringing essential utilities under greater public control, must all be funded under the same constraints faced by Starmer. Quite how remains an open question. The economy is front-and-center of this year’s conference, which takes place just weeks before the new chancellor delivers the first budget of the Burnham government, setting out the approach to taxation and spending. Burnham vowed to take “difficult decisions” on the economy earlier this month after official data showed a rise in inflation amid rising energy prices due to conflict in the Middle East. The latest inflation figures were a “concern,” Burnham said, but he also spoke of the “resilience” of the British economy. “It is going to be challenging, because the picture around the world is challenging, particularly the situation in the Middle East, and we will look carefully at all those things.” Party unity Burnham entered 10 Downing Street with a sizeable entourage of supporters, having secured the backing of 379 out of 403 Labour MPs. Mood within the party is still said to be chirpy and there is a lack of appetite to criticize the new leader, according to British media reports, but opposition is clearly growing in some quarters. Ahead of the Labour conference, Peter Kyle – who previously served as Starmer’s business secretary – said the government was not focused enough on economic growth and needed to act with “more urgency.” Asked by the BBC if there was enough focus on growth, Kyle said, “I don’t think there is and that isn’t a criticism – it is pointing to the potential that we have as a country and as a government.” He said the government must “feel the need for economic growth” as acutely as it does about ending social ills such as rough sleeping – a pointed reference to a key pledge Burnham made in his first speech as prime minister. Meanwhile, Housing Secretary Angela Rayner, who was deputy head of the Labour party under Starmer before her 2024 resignation, has called out a planned change to visa rules which would impact foreign social care workers. That led to Burnham’s culture secretary, Lisa Nandy, taking to the radio to voice her support for her boss. “I think the reason, frankly, that we had a change of leadership at the start of this year is because we all felt that people need to feel the change in their lives that we promised in 2024 much more quickly,” she told the BBC. The prime minister is “impatient for change, and he thinks big about the sort of change that the country needs,” she added. Burnham is also facing opposition from grassroots Labour groups over the government’s stance on the conflict in Gaza, with some demanding Burnham bans arms sales to Israel and introduces “wide-ranging” sanctions on the country. An early election? As mentioned, Burnham has already batted off the idea of an early general election. “No election anytime soon. I’m focused on the job as prime minister, doing what I said I would do,” he said last week. As it stands the next election must be called before August 2029. A strong election win would likely consolidate Burnham’s power and give him the mandate needed to push forward the policy changes set out at the beginning of his premiership. A failure to call an election could lead to accusations of weakness, as it did for former British leader Gordon Brown. After a successful start to his tenure, things went downhill for Brown in 2007 when he ducked a widely expected general election – a move then-Conservative leader David Cameron cast as a “humiliating retreat.” But an early election could also carry the risk of putting Labour’s falling support in opinion polls since the 2024 election under the spotlight, as Reform and Labour vie for the upper hand. Burnham is therefore in somewhat of a “Catch-22” over this decision. “The Labour Party are back in the lead. But are we in a situation where it would seem to make sense for Andy Burnham to go to the country anytime soon? Definitely not,” John Curtice, professor of politics at the University of Strathclyde and a leading polling expert, told Times Radio on Thursday. It’s clear which option Burnham would rather take, at least for now. “The time has come to draw a line, get the country looking forward, pulling together, people feeling a bit of hope in their lives again,” Burnham told the BBC. “That’s what I’m trying to do, and I hope to take it further in the coming period rather than putting people back into an election cycle.”

articles.title: Dennis Haskins, principal on TV’s ‘Saved by the Bell,’ dies at 75
articles.summary: The actor portrayed Richard Belding on the show, as well as in the spinoff series “Saved by the Bell: The New Class.”
articles.body: Dennis Haskins, the actor best known for his role as principal Richard Belding on the high school comedy series “Saved by the Bell,” has died, his agent said Monday. Haskins was 75. The cause and manner of death were unavailable. “It’s a tragic loss,” Jay Schachter, head of film and television for Stewart Talent in New York City, said in a statement. Haskins’ role on the show, which aired from 1989 to 1993, would come to define him for millions of fans. “Everyone loved Mr. Belding and those of us who got to know Dennis, loved him even more,” Schachter said. “He was a great person, and he loved, I mean absolutely LOVED his fans.” Haskins was born and raised in Chattanooga, Tennessee, and attended the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga, where he reported for the student newspaper, acted in campus productions and was a founding member of the community theater group known as the Harlequins, according to his university biography. As a young man, he worked as a music manager, agent and concert promoter and boasted Tom Jones and Gregg Allman among his clients, according to his IMDb bio. Early in his career, he landed appearances on TV’s “Magnum, P.I.” and “The Twilight Zone,” according to IMDb. His acting career was boosted by his portrayal of Mr. Belding on Disney Channel’s “Good Morning, Miss Bliss” in 1988, according to the university bio. The next year, NBC aired the show as “Saved by the Bell”; it ran until 1993. He reprised the role on “Saved by the Bell: The New Class,” which aired Saturday mornings from 1993 to 2000 on NBC. After the show’s end, he found work in several movies and television shows, including “It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia,” according to his university bio. Schachter said Haskins will be missed. “He was my client and dear friend for over 20 years, and I will miss him terribly,” he said. “I’m heartbroken.”
